clue.text: NT character, this person in Jerusalem

indicators.note: the words this person sit inside the name for Jerusalem

parts.note: Sion (Zion) is the hill of Jerusalem and a name for the city
the setter referring to themself gives me

explanation.surface: A New Testament figure, the speaker, is found in Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: NT is New Testament; Simeon held the infant Jesus in the Temple in Luke's gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: Simeon is the devout old man in Luke who blesses the baby Jesus, a New Testament figure.

clue.text: Christening's a do to be made fun of , so ___?

definitions.text: Christening's a do to be made fun of , so

indicators.note: making fun of the letters means mocking them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the S included
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests that even a baptism party is being mocked: has religion no respect left?
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of CHRISTENINGS and A DO rearrange into the indignant question, which the whole clue also prompts.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what an outraged person says when something holy, such as a baptism, is ridiculed.

clue.text: Ruler in angry mood over gold — tons gone missing

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed above the second
the tons letter disappears from the word for an angry mood

parts.note: a temper is a fit of anger
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A ruler in a rage over gold finds his tons of it gone.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign ruler of an empire.

clue.text: Little boy upset birds — there's an absence of contrition

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the little boy's name upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: Ron is a short boy's name, from Ronald
egrets are white herons

explanation.surface: A small lad has disturbed some birds and feels no remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no regrets means feeling no remorse, an absence of contrition.

clue.text: Spooner's "enjoyable snack" turns out to be a grand party

indicators.note: Spooner swaps the opening sounds of the two words of his phrase

parts.note: something enjoyable is fun
a bite is a snack

explanation.surface: What sounded like a tasty nibble turns out to be a big formal do.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of FUN BITE gives BUN FITE, spelt BUNFIGHT; a bunfight is British slang for a tea party or grand function.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunfight is informal British for a tea party or large official social function.

clue.text: Flannel from ex-PM, one gone with craving to be ascendant

indicators.note: the one letter leaves the former prime minister's name

parts.note: Tony Blair was UK prime minister 1997-2007
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, reads the word for craving upwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A former prime minister's smooth talk comes from a craving to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel is British slang for evasive smooth talk, the same as blarney or flattering nonsense.

clue.text: Lawson wanting a new direction, finally, for the country

indicators.note: one compass-style direction, left, is swapped for another, right
the change happens at the last letter

parts.note: Nigel Lawson was a UK Chancellor of the Exchequer

explanation.surface: Lawson heads off a different way at the end, bound for an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) at the end of NIGEL becomes R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked West African nation.

clue.text: Outside body very involved in rioting — bad, not good

indicators.note: the letter for very gets wrapped up inside the rest
the remaining letters of rioting go bad, rearranged
the good letter is removed from rioting

explanation.surface: Riots that are extremely bad and not good spill outside the body politic.
explanation.walkthrough: RIOTING without G is RIOTIN; 'bad' rearranges it to INITRO, and 'involved in' puts V inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In vitro, Latin for in glass, describes processes carried out outside a living organism, in a test tube.

clue.text: Minutes at a meeting will be that important

definitions.text: Minutes at a meeting will be that important

parts.words: Minutes at a meeting will be that important
parts.note: the minutes of the last meeting are traditionally the first item listed on the order of business

explanation.definitionFit: A top priority is a matter listed near the top of a meeting's order of business, where the minutes always come.

clue.text: Mantra of 2012 with sporting arenas pioneering it

indicators.note: sporting suggests the letters frolic about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The 2012 motto was paired with sports stadiums leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The London 2012 Olympics used this slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the official slogan of the London 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

clue.text: Force-feeding provided — time to replace energy

indicators.note: the time word takes the place of the energy letter

parts.note: gave means provided
E is the symbol for energy
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Force-feeding was supplied when it was time to swap out energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gavage is the technical term for forcing food into the stomach, as with geese for foie gras.

clue.text: An indication of a division in high places

definitions.text: An indication of a division in high places

parts.words: An indication of a division in high places
parts.note: the zodiac divides the heavens into twelve parts, each with its own symbol

explanation.definitionFit: Each zodiacal sign marks one twelfth of the sky, a division of the heavens.

clue.text: See 9
Run through church past pillar

indicators.note: the church comes after the pillar

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone runs through the church past a column.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to stab or run something through.

clue.text: Youngster carrying gun somewhere west of Newport

indicators.note: the youngster holds the weapon inside

parts.note: a youth is a young person
an arm is a weapon such as a gun

explanation.surface: A young man is carrying a firearm somewhere west of a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Newport here is the main town of the Isle of Wight, not the Welsh city; Yarmouth is a port to its west on the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarmouth is a small harbour town on the Isle of Wight, lying west of its county town.

clue.text: Bent judge pretended to protect what's right

indicators.note: the two words shelter the right letter between them

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a match
acted means pretended
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A crooked judge feigned defending what is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Light that is refracted is bent as it passes between media.

clue.text: Adult fails, admitting transgression's return — and worries a lot

parts.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: the word for fails lets the turned sin into it

parts.note: a machine that goes has given out or failed

indicators.note: the transgression comes back, read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a transgression

explanation.surface: A grown-up falters, confessing a sin has come back, and frets heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails' reads as giving up, but here a thing that goes has broken down; 'return' reverses the sin before 'admitting' takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to worry intensely over something.

clue.text: Soothing remedy never working, popular for swallowing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters swallow the popular word
working means the letters of never are worked into a new order

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A calming medicine never works, yet people keep taking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' scrambles the never letters to the word for courage, and 'for swallowing' makes them enclose the word for popular.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervine is a medicine that calms the nerves, a soothing tonic.

clue.text: Red mark that's deadly, not half

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: only half of the word for deadly is kept

parts.note: lethal means deadly

explanation.surface: A red mark that would be fatal, but only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of LETHAL, LET, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright shade of red.

clue.text: Expression of desires — any number will fade away

indicators.note: the number letter vanishes from the word for desires

parts.note: fancies are desires
N stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: Desires show on the face, but any number of them will fade.
explanation.definitionFit: Facies is a technical term for a face's appearance or facial expression, especially in medicine.

clue.text: The French occupying sheds or big buildings

indicators.note: the French article moves in and sits inside the word for sheds

parts.note: a snake casts or sheds its skin
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The French have taken over sheds or larger buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Castles are large fortified buildings.

clue.text: Artist in European country joins volunteers to produce opera

indicators.note: the volunteers attach to the end
the artist goes inside the country

parts.note: Latvia is a Baltic state
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A painter in a Baltic country teams up with volunteers to stage an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: La Traviata is Verdi's opera about the courtesan Violetta.

clue.text: Very old visitor ignoring street fashion

indicators.note: the street letters are left out of the visitor word

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A very old visitor pays no attention to street style.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in vogue is in fashion; vogue is the prevailing style.

clue.text: See 11
Eg misdialling to get Queen on phone

indicators.note: the Queen sits before the phone in the across entry

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina
to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: Dialling the wrong number to reach the monarch on the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Misdialling is an example of making a mistake, going wrong.

clue.text: Much less neglected

definitions.meaning: used as in not to mention, still less

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both still less (he can't walk, never mind run) and left undisturbed or ignored.

clue.text: Disciple of the modern era, the man torn apart

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the modern era
he is the man
rent means torn

explanation.surface: A follower of today's age sees the man ripped to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter of a cause or teacher.

clue.text: Gloomy mug laid into by sergeant major

indicators.note: the sergeant major gets inside the word for mug

parts.note: dial is slang for face, like mug

explanation.surface: A miserable face is set upon by a drill sergeant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means gloomy and depressing.
